assumptions: Printed means used as deterministic plug-in aggregates; outputs are conditional, not exact empirical effects.
The follow-up respondents are subsets of the N=41 baseline cohort and their baseline means refer to those same respondents, as stated in the motor-results paragraphs.
Missing motor scores lie within 0–25; baseline and missing-outcome mean partitions are handled separately.
No missing-at-random assumption is imposed for scale bounds.
Every missing-outcome scenario is hypothetical; no individual records are constructed.
A single-arm mean change cannot identify a causal effect, disease modification, cure or a severe-persistent-adult effect.
